metadata.chapter_subtitle: Predicting when and where satellites are visible from the ground

inventory.summary: The visibility chapter had good geometric substance but needed explicit onboarding so readers could distinguish position, local horizon, and line-of-sight questions before the vector algebra began.
issues: The chapter opened quickly into vector geometry without a learner-facing setup block.
The conceptual difference between being nearby on Earth and being visible above the horizon needed stronger emphasis.
The topic-library sequence needed consistent onboarding across the orbital mechanics set.

rewrite.summary: Added a clearer reader ramp and preserved the core line-of-sight derivation and overpass geometry.
editor_notes: Added a Before You Start section to separate the geometric objects involved.
Kept the vector derivations because they fit the volume once the entry is gentler.
Used the onboarding to tie the chapter more directly to real overpass prediction.

qa_review.summary: The chapter now introduces visibility geometry at a fairer pace while maintaining correct vector and angle relationships.

repair.summary: The main repair was pedagogical: a stronger conceptual setup before the formal geometry.
actions_taken: Added a Before You Start section.
Preserved the worked vector-geometry treatment and visibility conditions.

design_review.summary: The chapter already uses figures and geometry explainers appropriately, and the added onboarding improves interpretation of those tools.
improvements_made: Added prerequisite framing before the main derivation.
Retained the chapter's applied overpass and angle-explainer structure.
Improved interpretive support around the meaning of elevation and azimuth.
